messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] GeoDNS anomaly detected — elevated NXDOMAIN rate from Cloudflare resolvers in eu-west-1. Metric: dns_nxdomain_rate > 7% for last 5m. Affected service: api.redwood.ai (edge). Severity: SEV2. Pager: on-call SRE. Runbook: geo-dns -> 'GeoDNS failover' (link).

alice-smith: picking this up — reading alerts and top-traffic graphs now. @raj-patel are you around for Cloudflare/Route53 routing details?

raj-patel: here. seeing a spike in NXDOMAINs from a subset of CF resolver ASN range. dig from our probes shows inconsistent answers from Cloudflare in eu-west-1.

maya-kim: customer-reports: two large tenants in EU reported 502s and 5xx when contacting chat endpoints ~10m ago. Support is collecting traces.

alice-smith: quick triage: 1) confirm if Route53 answers are consistent 2) decide temporary mitigation (force Route53 fallback / increase weight) 3) assess impact and notify customers.

raj-patel: running digs from multiple egress points:
```
# probe eu-west-1 -> cloudflare resolver
$ dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.ai A +short
;; -> sometimes returns NXDOMAIN, sometimes ip x.x.x.x

# route53 authoritative answer
$ dig @ns-aws-route53 api.redwood.ai A +short
x.x.x.x
```
Output: Cloudflare answers inconsistent across probes, Route53 authoritative is stable.

eva-bernal: TL;DR: Cloudflare's resolver edge seems to be returning stale/inconsistent cache entries for some POPs. Might be propagation issue or resolver outage.

alice-smith: mitigation options: a) temporarily prefer Route53 by lowering Cloudflare weight in GeoDNS config; b) increase TTL on authoritative records (might not help immediately); c) add health-checker override to mark CF POPs unhealthy. Thoughts?

raj-patel: we can flip GeoDNS to Route53-only for eu-west-1 origin mapping (quick change in control plane). That should cut the NXDOMAIN incidence for new lookups within ~time-to-live (we're using low TTL ~30s currently). I can push the change if SRE approves.

maya-kim: ops: if we make that change, notify SEs and customer success — customers already opening tickets. Also prepare rollback plan.

alice-smith: approved. @raj-patel make the change and post the exact ops command. I'll monitor metrics and update status.

raj-patel: executing now. Pushing GeoDNS policy update: set primary -> Route53 for eu-west-1, weight 100, fallback disabled.

opsbot: ACTION: geo-dns:update executed by raj-patel at 2026-03-15T22:14:12Z. Change ID: gd-20260315-1123.

alice-smith: monitoring 1m windows. dns_nxdomain_rate dropping?

raj-patel: initial: 7.8% -> 1.1% after 45s. Some residual clients with cached NXDOMAIN will fail for TTL window.

incident-bot: Status update: Impact reduced from SEV2 -> SEV3 candidate. Continue monitoring for 30m before declaring mitigated.

maya-kim: customer communication draft: "We identified a DNS resolution issue affecting some EU queries. We applied a routing change to prefer Route53 which significantly reduced errors; investigating root cause with Cloudflare. We'll update in 30 minutes." Approve? :loudspeaker:

eva-bernal: approve, add note: "no data leakage, only resolution errors".

alice-smith: send now. @maya-kim can you post to status page and notify support teams?

maya-kim: posted to status.redwood.ai and notified CS slack channel.

tony-lee: Ops note: If we see bounce back or increased latency after change, revert to previous weighted config and open escalation with CF. Also: record dig logs from failing clients and file with Cloudflare support.

raj-patel: collecting per-probe dig traces and attaching to ticket. Command I used to capture noisy resolvers:
```bash
for r in $(cat eu-probes.txt); do dig @$r api.redwood.ai ANY +short >> /tmp/dig-${r}.log; done
```
I'll upload compressed logs to the incident bundle.

alice-smith: good. Next: Pager handoff at 23:00 UTC — I'm on until then then handing to eva. @eva-bernal can you take after 23:00?

eva-bernal: I can. I'll be online and will review the change history and CF ticket.

incident-bot: [PAGER] handoff scheduled: alice-smith -> eva-bernal at 2026-03-15T23:00:00Z.

maya-kim: CS: two enterprise customers (AcmeCorp, Tradely) reported intermittent failures. I've opened high-priority support threads and notified their TAMs. No SLA misses recorded yet but monitoring closely.

alice-smith: temporary mitigation seems stable for now. Action items captured:
- raj-patel: upload dig logs and raise ticket with Cloudflare (ID TBD)
- eva-bernal: assume on-call at 23:00 UTC and keep monitoring for 2h
- maya-kim: customer comms and support coordination
- alice-smith: draft postmortem template after the incident closes

opsbot: Incident record created: INC-20260315-042. Severity: SEV2 (initial) -> SEV3 (mitigated). Linked change: gd-20260315-1123.

raj-patel: Cloudflare ticket opened: CF-TKT-987654. Summary: resolver POP in eu-west-1 returning inconsistent NXDOMAINs for api.redwood.ai. Attached dig logs + timestamps. Awaiting CF response.

eva-bernal: took over on-call at 23:00. Reviewing metrics and CF ticket. DNS NXDOMAIN rate holding ~0.8% (baseline ~0.1%). Watching for regressions.

maya-kim: update from CS: AcmeCorp still sees a small fraction of failures (~2% requests in last 10m). They want ETA. I told them we're monitoring and have applied fallback; next update in 30m.

alice-smith: recommended: increase TTL temporarily to 60s to reduce churn while CF investigates? That would slow propagation of any future changes though. Leaning against unless we see oscillation.

raj-patel: agree — keep TTL low for now to allow quick rollback if CF fixes.

incident-bot: Scheduled check in 30m. Please update incident channel with any change.

eva-bernal: Cloudflare replied: investigating internal cache invalidation; suspect partial cache corruption on subset of resolvers. They requested sample dig logs and timestamps (which we already provided). CF estimates 1-2 hours for deeper diagnosis.

maya-kim: CS update sent to customers: CF investigating; we applied Route53 fallback; monitoring. No ETA beyond CF's 1-2h. Customers acknowledged.

alice-smith: summary before I drop: mitigation applied and holding. Please: keep an eye on NXDOMAIN metric and latency. If it rises >2% -> re-escalate and consider full failover for EU region. Postmortem will capture timeline and action items.

eva-bernal: noted. I'll continue watching and will add notes to the incident record.

opsbot: Incident INC-20260315-042 — status: monitoring. Owners: SRE (eva-bernal), Network (raj-patel), Support (maya-kim).

alice-smith: thanks team — handing off.

alice-smith: handoff complete. Leaving channel. :wave:

incident-bot: Thread closed for active operators at 2026-03-16T00:05:00Z, monitoring continues. Remind: postmortem required if incident worsened or customer impact >5 minutes for enterprise customers.

eva-bernal: filing initial incident notes and scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Attendees: SRE, Network, Support, Product.

maya-kim: will include customer timeline and support escalations in postmortem.

raj-patel: will include Cloudflare ticket ID and dig logs.

incident-bot: Final visible note: Mitigation applied (Route53 preference), impact reduced. Follow-up: postmortem + Cloudflare RCA to be attached to incident record.
